Summarize a Hammel population

Source: R/hammel_population.R
summary.hammel_population.Rd

Summary method for class "hammel_population"

Usage

# S3 method for class 'hammel_population'
summary(object, interval_pyramid = 5, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.hammel_population'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

an object of class "hammel_population", usually the result of a call to run_simulation.

interval_pyramid

length of age intervals used for drawing population pyramid

...

further arguments passed on from other methods.

x

A summary.hammel_population object returned by summary.hammel_population().

Value

summary() returns an object of class summary.hammel_population containing:

first_time

The earliest recorded birth time, in years.

end_time

The population's reference time, in years.

persons_alive

The number of persons alive at the reference time.

n_births

The number of recorded persons with a birth time, including persons in the starting population.

n_births_u

The number of retained unrealized birth records, or NA when no unrealized birth table is present.

n_deaths

The number of recorded persons with a death time.

n_unions

The number of recorded union episodes, including ended unions.

n_dissolutions

The number of union episodes with end reason "dissolution".

age_counts

A tibble of living male and female counts by five-year age group, with columns age, male, and female.

simulation

A list describing the latest simulation run, with start and end times in years and living population counts pop_size_start and pop_size_end, or NULL when no simulation metadata is present.

group_counts

A named list of tibbles, one per declared group dimension, or NULL when no groups are declared. Each tibble contains category, count, and percent for the living population at the reference time, including declared categories with zero members. Percentages are on a 0–100 scale and are NaN when the dimension's total living count is zero.

print() displays the summary, group counts when present, and a text population pyramid, returning its input invisibly. Pyramid bars share a common scale across both sexes.

Examples


# get summary of starting population
population <- generate_uniform_population(1000)
summary(population)
#> 
#> ── Population ──
#> 
#> • First date: -69.885
#> • End time: 0
#> • Persons alive at end time: 1000
#> • Total births: 1000
#> • Total deaths: 0
#> • Total unions: 0
#> • Total dissolutions: 0
#> 
#> ── Living population by age and sex 
#>                      Male     Age     Female                   
#>       ################### |  65-69  | ################         
#>       ################### |  60-64  | ###########              
#>          ################ |  55-59  | #############            
#>        ################## |  50-54  | ###################      
#>              ############ |  45-49  | ################         
#>         ################# |  40-44  | ##############           
#>        ################## |  35-39  | ############             
#>         ################# |  30-34  | #########################
#>        ################## |  25-29  | ####################     
#>           ############### |  20-24  | ###############          
#>      #################### |  15-19  | ###############          
#>       ################### |  10-14  | ############             
#>        ################## |   5-9   | #################        
#>         ################# |   0-4   | ###################      

# get summary of simulatied population
model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_population(population) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility) |>
  set_union_formation("on_demand")
result <- run_simulation(model, years = 50, seed = 42)
summary(result)
